title: Approach to Esophageal Manometry in Invasive Hemodynamic Determinations
one_line_summary: Invasive catheterization measurements can **significantly** overestimate cardiac filling pressures when intrathoracic pressure is elevated; esophageal manometry allows determination of true transmural pressure to avoid misdiagnosis and inappropriate therapy.
key_pearls: - Transmural pressure (*P_tm* = *P_im* - *P_em*) represents true cardiac distending pressure; standard catheters measure intramural pressure (*P_im*), which overestimates preload when extramural pleural pressure (*P_pl*) is elevated.
- Esophageal pressure (*P_es*) serves as a surrogate for *P_pl* in mid-dependent thoracic zones directly posterior to the left atrium, enabling calculation of *P_es*-adjusted transmural pressures.

- Preload assessment requires end-expiratory, end-diastolic (pre-*c*-wave) measurements, whereas organ congestion assessment is best evaluated using digital time-averaged (mean) pressures across the respiratory cycle.

- High-yield scenarios for esophageal balloon placement include elevated filling pressures (RAP or PAWP **15-20 mm Hg**), large respiratory oscillations (**>10 mm Hg** RAP or **>15 mm Hg** PAWP), and clinical/imaging discordance with catheter values.

- In severe obesity or high PEEP, end-expiratory *P_es* can exceed **10 mm Hg**; subtracting *P_es* from measured PAWP prevents misclassifying precapillary pulmonary hypertension as postcapillary disease.

sections.heading: Physiologic Principles: Intramural, Extramural, and Transmural Pressures
sections.content:
- Cardiovascular chambers act as distensible spheres where true preload is defined by transmural pressure (*P_tm* = *P_im* - *P_em*).
- Intramural pressure (*P_im*) is the intravascular pressure measured directly by fluid-filled catheters.
- Extramural pressure (*P_em*) of the heart is pericardial pressure, which under normal conditions mirrors pleural pressure (*P_pl*).
- Pericardial pressure increases independent of *P_pl* in **cardiac tamponade**, **constrictive pericarditis**, and **pericardial restraint** from acute volume overload.
- Pleural pressure (*P_pl*) is elevated in **class III obesity**, **intraabdominal hypertension**, **tension pneumothorax**, active exhalation, and during **positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP)**.
section_pearls: Catheter readings reflect intramural pressure only, which overestimates true preload in conditions of elevated intrathoracic pressure.
Normal end-expiratory pleural pressure is near zero but is substantially elevated in severe obesity.

sections.heading: Clinical Applications: Preload Assessment versus Venous Congestion
sections.content:
- For **ventricular preload assessment**, measure end-expiratory, end-diastolic pressures at the base of the *c*-wave or middle of the *a*-wave.
- For **systemic venous congestion**, measure the digital time-averaged mean right atrial pressure (RAP) across the complete respiratory cycle.
- For **pulmonary venous congestion**, evaluate *P_es*-adjusted mean PAWP (mean PAWP minus mean *P_es*) to capture the congestive impact of large *v*-waves.
- Relying solely on end-diastolic PAWP can underestimate total pulmonary venous congestion when **significant** *v*-waves are present.
section_pearls: Preload determination requires end-diastolic timing at end-expiration, whereas organ congestion relies on time-averaged mean pressures.
P_es-adjusted mean PAWP provides the most accurate physiologic representation of pulmonary vascular congestion.

sections.heading: Indications and High-Yield Scenarios for Esophageal Manometry
sections.content:
- Indicated when pretest probability of elevated *P_pl* is high and adjusting pressures alters clinical diagnosis or therapy.
- Indication 1: Elevated measured filling pressures (RAP or PAWP approximately **15 to 20 mm Hg**).
- Indication 2: Large respiratory oscillations in pressure waveforms (end-expiratory vs end-inspiratory difference **>10 mm Hg** for RAP or **>15 mm Hg** for PAWP).
- Indication 3: Discordance between noninvasive/clinical data and invasive hemodynamics (e.g., measured PAWP **>20 mm Hg** without radiographic pulmonary edema).
- Rule of thumb: Low measured end-expiratory RAP (e.g., **3 mm Hg**) rules out **significantly** elevated end-expiratory *P_pl*, as higher *P_pl* would imply an implausible negative transmural pressure.
section_pearls: Examine for esophageal manometry if respiratory pressure swings exceed 10 mm Hg in RAP or 15 mm Hg in PAWP.
Low intramural RAP effectively excludes significant elevation of end-expiratory pleural pressure.

sections.heading: Technique, Protocol, and Validation of Esophageal Balloon Placement
sections.content:
- Transducer preparation: Zero all pressure transducers to atmosphere at the **fourth intercostal space, mid-axillary line**.
- Insertion: Pass a **5F balloon catheter** nasally (or orally in ventilated patients) to a depth of **35 to 45 cm** from the nares.
- Positioning: In the mid-esophagus, adjust position until maximal respiratory pressure deflections are observed; inflate balloon with **1 to 2 mL** of air.
- Validation in spontaneous breathing: Perform a dynamic airway occlusion test where changes in airway pressure during occlusion are mirrored by *P_es*.
- Validation in mechanical ventilation: Apply external chest wall compression during an expiratory pause to verify concurrent shifts in airway pressure and *P_es*.
- Waveform confirmation: Confirm negative deflections during inhalation and positive deflections with exhalation; small sharp oscillations correspond to the *T-wave*.
section_pearls: Mid-esophageal balloon placement positions the sensor adjacent to the left atrium for optimal local pleural pressure estimation.
Avoid balloon overinflation to prevent baseline pressure measurement artifacts.

sections.heading: PEEP Interactions, Positional Dynamics, and Limitations of Alternative Surrogates
sections.content:
- Approximately **33% to 50%** of applied PEEP is transmitted to intramural vascular pressures, depending on respiratory system mechanics.
- High PEEP (**>10 cmH2O**) can cause overestimation of transmural PAWP due to creation of West Zone 1 or Zone 2 conditions.
- Upright positioning decreases intrathoracic pressure; in patients with obesity, **70%** of the upright drop in pulmonary vascular pressures is driven by a drop in *P_es*.
- Threshold inflation airway pressure (*PAO-Thr*) reflects ventral nondependent pleural pressure and correlates poorly with pleural pressure surrounding the left atrium.
- Cadaveric studies demonstrate that *P_es* measures pleural pressure in dependent-to-middle lung zones, making it an ideal surrogate for peri-cardiac pleural pressure.
section_pearls: Between one-third and one-half of applied PEEP transmits directly into intramural cardiac pressures.
PAO-Thr reflects non-dependent ventral pleural pressure, whereas P_es accurately reflects mid-chest peri-atrial pleural pressure.

strengths_limitations:
- **Strengths**: Synthesizes complex heart-lung interactions into clear clinical paradigms, provides a detailed bedside protocol for esophageal manometry, and justifies esophageal pressure monitoring using anatomical and cadaveric validation data.
- **Limitations**: Lack of large prospective clinical outcome trials demonstrating that P_es-guided hemodynamic therapy improves patient **survival** or clinical outcomes.

drugs_doses.indication: Nasal anesthesia prior to esophageal balloon catheter insertion
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Local mucosal irritation, rare systemic toxicity

drugs_doses.indication: Oropharyngeal anesthesia prior to esophageal balloon catheter insertion
